title: RealGen: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Controllable Traffic Scenarios

control_signal.value: A few template scenarios or behavior tags (e.g. left turn, lane change, overtaking, hand-made crash templates) that define which behaviors are retrieved and combined.

control_mechanism.value: Retrieval-based in-context learning: KNN retrieves similar behavior embeddings from a contrastive latent space, and a trained combiner fuses them with map and initial positions to generate; gradient-free.

base_model.value: Transformer autoencoder with spatial-temporal behavior encoder, map encoder and initial-position encoder, contrastive loss on behavior embeddings, plus a combiner with frozen encoder/decoder.

datasets.value: nuScenes, with 1349 manually tagged template scenarios for six behavior tags; crash templates informed by NHTSA crash reports; Autobots used for downstream test.

metrics.value: MMD of velocity and heading, mADE, mFDE, scene collision rate, off-road rate; collision rate for crash templates; human A/B preference and 0-5 score versus LCTGen.

controllability_evidence.value: Human evaluation: RealGen preferred 81.8 to 100.0% across five categories; scores 3.94 to 4.27 versus LCTGen 2.0 to 2.42. Crash-template generation reported with collision rate.

stated_limitations.value: Behavior encoder models only agent trajectories and ignores interactions between agents and lane maps in complex behaviors.

notes: Table 3 numbers (AE-R 0.92, R 0.83, RealGen 0.59) look inconsistent with the text claiming RealGen has the highest collision rate; column order may be garbled, so no collision number is quoted. Authors say controllability has no automatic metric.
